bugs.summary: [GEO-Category] Prompt detail ranking lists the same brand several times instead of folding products into their brand family

description.description: In the prompt detail panel of a Visibility prompt, the "Ranking - {Engine}" list shows the same brand on several rows. The detail API returns one ranking row per product, with the product in `name` (e.g. "Toyota Prius") and the brand in `family` ("Toyota"); the panel prints `family` on every row without folding the rows, so a brand with several products is listed several times and the positions are misleading. The panel title is built from the first row's `name` ("Toyota Prius's Position"), which names a product instead of the brand (the product-name title already shows on production; the duplicated rows do not, since the production API has no `family` field yet). Scope on staging: 70 of the 100 Visibility prompt × engine pairs of Toyota > Voitures hybrides (ChatGPT 22/25, Gemini 23/25, Perplexity 17/25, Grok 8/25), in English, French and Spanish prompts.
steps: Open the Toyota analysis on staging (organisation QA-GEO) > category "Voitures hybrides" > Prompts Analysis, Visibility tab (Last 7 days, All Countries).
Click the prompt "Best hybrid cars?" (United States).
In the detail panel, select the ChatGPT engine tab.
Read the "Ranking - ChatGPT" list and the panel title.
description.expected: One entry per brand family at the position of its first mention, with the name the engine wrote shown below it when it differs (GEO-1553 AC3: "they fold into one entry for the brand at the position of its first mention"; GEO-1498, 27 Oct: "it shows the brand family, as the questions table does since GEO-1530, with the name the engine wrote below it when it differs"). The panel title names the brand. — to confirm
description.actual: Toyota appears at #2, #4, #6 and #7 (API: Toyota Prius, Toyota Camry Hybrid, Toyota Corolla Hybrid, Toyota Crown) and Hyundai at #3, #5 and #9 (Hyundai Elantra Hybrid, Hyundai Sonata Hybrid, Hyundai Ioniq Hybrid). The title reads "Toyota Prius's Position".
